title: Trump and Jim Cramer Defend SpaceX as Musk Wants to Enter the Telecom Market
detail:
Trump and Jim Cramer Defend SpaceX as Musk Wants to Enter the Telecom Market
Lockridge Okoth

Donald Trump and Jim Cramer both defended SpaceX on Monday, after reports that Elon Musk's company is in talks to buy Boost Mobile, a US phone carrier with about 7 million customers.

The support lands with SpaceX stock near $137 on Monday, barely above its $135 initial public offering (IPO) price. A Boost deal, Tuesday's midterm elections, and a December share unlock will shape what shareholders face next.

SpaceX Stock (SPCX) Performance. Source: Yahoo Finance
What a Boost Mobile Deal Would Give SpaceX

SpaceX is talking to EchoStar (ECHO) about buying Boost Mobile, or renting its network. Musk wants a full US phone service that pairs Starlink satellites with ground towers.

He first asked AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile for network access. Reports indicate that all three refused.

Cramer, the CNBC host, said Boost would settle doubts about SpaceX's reach.

"SpaceX may have a ton of stock coming to market but this Boost Mobile possibility (Echostar owned) would end any question that it doesn't have the reach to compete," he said.

Under the IPO terms, many early investors agreed to a staggered 180-day lockup, a ban on selling, which starts to lift in December.

EchoStar holders are already reacting. The stock rose 6.5% before Monday's open. In September 2025, it jumped about 19% when SpaceX agreed to buy EchoStar's airwaves for $17 billion.

EchoStar Stock (ECHO) Price Performance. Source: Yahoo Finance

The catch is that Boost rents its network from AT&T and T-Mobile. Those leases may not pass to a new owner, so the carriers that rejected Musk could still block access. No deal has been reached.

Trump Steps In For SpaceX

Trump said Musk must be protected if Democrats put SpaceX at risk. He told Fox Business on October 24 that "Elon has done nothing wrong."

Democrats have discussed probing Musk's federal contracts if they win Congress on Tuesday. Rep. Zoe Lofgren, the top Democrat on the House Science Committee, has pointed to conflicts of interest, The Hill reported.

Musk has spent about $276 million helping Republicans since July.

However, Trump's support has flipped before. In June 2025, he threatened to end Musk's government contracts, and Tesla shares fell about 16% that day.

Neither defense addressed Friday's 6.4% drop, which came during a broad tech selloff over AI spending, according to the Associated Press.

The swing also reaches crypto platforms that offer tokenized SpaceX shares. Election results, carrier approval, and December's unlocks now set the next test for SpaceX stock.

Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) dived 11% on Monday on competition concerns following reports that SpaceX is in talks with EchoStar about buying Boost Mobile to gain access to its network.

According to a report from The Washington Post, SpaceX discussed a deal with EchoStar about buying Boost Mobile or gaining access to its network to launch its own wireless service. A possible deal would strengthen SpaceX's direct-to-device ambitions and raise pressure on AST SpaceMobile's model. ECHO stock was trading 2% higher at the time of writing.

ASTS Model Under Pressure

AST SpaceMobile is building a network of satellites designed to work hand-in-hand with existing wireless carriers. Rather than competing head-on as a standalone phone service, the company partners with operators such as AT&T (T) and Verizon (VZ).

SpaceX, meanwhile, is seeking to establish itself as a standalone wireless competitor and recently acquired low-band spectrum that will help integrate its Starlink satellites into what CEO Elon Musk has described as a "major mobile carrier."

Last month, Bloomberg also reported that SpaceX is pursuing agreements for a minimum of 80,000 cell sites across the United States as it advances plans to build a fourth nationwide wireless carrier. The report said that SpaceX is in discussions with at least one major cellular infrastructure company and that Crown Castle Inc. (CCI), among the largest U.S. owners of cellular towers alongside American Tower (AMT) and Vertical Bridge, was also approached for the purpose.

How Did ASTS, ECHO Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ASTS and SPCX stock stayed within the 'bearish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'low' levels.

Meanwhile, sentiment around ECHO stock jumped from 'bearish' to 'bullish' territory.

SpaceX Eyes Boost Mobile to Fast-Track Wireless, Undercutting Verizon's "4-6 Years" Estimate ©RiverNorthPhotography from Getty Images Signature metamorworks from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

The Washington Post reported that SpaceX is in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile or get access to its network. Boost had 7.38 million wireless subscribers at the end of the second quarter.

A deal would give SpaceX the customers and retail operation that Verizon's CEO counted in his four-to-six-year estimate, so its threat to Verizon's and AT&T's pricing would arrive sooner.

Analysts expect revenue at both Verizon and AT&T to grow less than 2% a year through 2028, which leaves little room to absorb a price war.

Boost's network leases may need AT&T's and T-Mobile's approval to change hands, so the terms of any deal are the thing to watch.

SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) may have found a shortcut past the timeline Verizon (VZ:NYSE) set for it.

On Monday the Washington Post reported that SpaceX is in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile or get access to its network. The paper cited people familiar with the negotiations. Elon Musk talked about a deal with EchoStar Chairman Charlie Ergen himself last month.

Boost had 7.38 million wireless subscribers at the end of the second quarter. It serves them on capacity it leases from AT&T (T:NYSE) and T-Mobile.

Four to six years, or two to three

Last Monday, on Verizon's third-quarter call, CEO Dan Schulman explained why SpaceX is no near-term threat. He said building a carrier network would take "a minimum of four to six years" and cost "somewhere between $300 billion and $500 billion." And the network was only part of it:

"Then they need to build retail, customer service, back office systems, et cetera."

Musk replied on X that it "will take 2 or 3 years."

Up to now, the argument over Musk's two-to-three-year timeline assumed SpaceX would build everything itself. With Boost, SpaceX could buy the second half of Schulman's list: a brand, millions of paying customers and the operation that already serves them.

The rest of the board is filling in

SpaceX is assembling the network too. In October it agreed to an $8 billion spectrum deal, on top of EchoStar spectrum the FCC approved in May. Bloomberg reported last month that SpaceX is in talks for at least 80,000 cell sites, and TD Cowen put the cost of that network at more than $80 billion. That's well short of Schulman's range.

AST SpaceMobile Sinks 10% as SpaceX Rises 2% on Reported Talks to Buy Boost Mobile ©Oleksii Mach, Leung Cho Pan via Canva
Key Takeaways

AST SpaceMobile fell 10% today on a report that SpaceX is in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile.

Boost would let SpaceX sell phone service directly, against AT&T and Verizon, AST's US carrier partners.

AT&T and Verizon have more to lose than AST, whose bigger risk is its own launch pace.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ) stock fell 10% today after The Washington Post reported that SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) is in talks to buy Boost Mobile from EchoStar (ECHO:NASDAQ), or to use its network.

SpaceX rose 2% on the report. Neither company has confirmed a deal.

Boost would give Starlink a ground network to sell phone service straight to US subscribers, making SpaceX a head-on rival to AT&T (T:NYSE) and Verizon (VZ:NYSE), AST's US carrier partners.

SpaceX wants to be a carrier

On SpaceX's Aug. 4 call, COO Gwynne Shotwell said she expects Starlink Mobile to "acquire quite a few" customers from the national carriers.

AST plans to earn its phone revenue through those carriers, and analysts expect it to take off once service starts:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)
The carriers have more to lose

Wireless made 96.9% of AT&T's segment operating income in 2025. Boost runs partly on capacity leased from AT&T, which would be renting its network to a new rival. Verizon just posted 406,000 postpaid phone net adds, its best third quarter in five years.

So I'd expect both to lean harder on AST's satellites. AT&T isn't backing away: today, it and AST announced what they believe is "the industry's first successful handoff" between a ground network and AST's satellites. And Verizon has a $45 million contingent prepayment lined up for AST.

TIKR tracks 13 analysts on AST SpaceMobile. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on AST SpaceMobile, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See AST SpaceMobile's Analyst Ratings

Launch dates, please

AST's forward price-to-sales multiple was 39x at Friday's close, below its five-year average of 60x:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): forward (NTM) price/sales, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's drop takes it lower, but that's still a price for a fast ramp. AST has 12 BlueBirds in orbit, against the 45 to 60 it needs for continuous service, and it hasn't launched since Aug. 5. And analysts expect free cash flow to stay deeply negative through 2028:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): free cash flow, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

That works out to about $3.2 billion still to burn from July through 2028, against over $3.7 billion of pro forma cash at June 30. A thin cushion, with SpaceX moving this fast.

AST's real risk is its own launch schedule, so I want firm dates for BlueBirds 14 to 16 in next week's report. Of course, a signed SpaceX-EchoStar deal would give AST one more reason to hurry.

SpaceX Gains 4% on Reported Boost Mobile Talks That Could Give It "The Reach to Compete" ©NASA/Kim Shiflett via Canva
Key Takeaways

SpaceX shares rose 4% today on a report that it's in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile or use its network.

A deal would hand Starlink Mobile millions of subscribers more than a year before SpaceX's own service is due.

Boost leases its network from AT&T and T-Mobile, and T-Mobile's CEO has ruled out a network deal with SpaceX.

Watch for any word from EchoStar or the carriers on Boost's leases.

SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) shares are up 4% today after The Washington Post reported that the company is in talks to buy Boost Mobile from EchoStar (ECHO:NASDAQ), or to use its network. Boost leases that network from AT&T (T:NYSE) and T-Mobile (TMUS:NASDAQ).

Jim Cramer, host of CNBC's Mad Money, posted on X that the Boost possibility "would end any question that it doesn't have the reach to compete."

A head start for Starlink Mobile

EchoStar's wireless business ended June with 7.4 million subscribers. That's more than half the 13.6 million Starlink consumer subscribers SpaceX had at the end of September.

SpaceX now expects its own next-generation Starlink Mobile service in early 2028, later than the end of 2027 it pointed to in August.

AT&T and T-Mobile hold the keys

The Post reported that Musk asked the big carriers for network access and was turned down, and that Boost's leases may not pass to a new owner without their approval.

"I see no room for an MVNO with SpaceX," T-Mobile CEO Srini Gopalan said on its Oct. 28 earnings call. It has reason to be wary: its postpaid account churn rose to 1.09% in the third quarter from 0.97% a year earlier.

AT&T is in a stronger spot, with postpaid phone churn of 0.92% in the third quarter and a raised 2026 adjusted EPS outlook. Does Boost's contract give it the chance to say no again?

EchoStar has the least to lose. Analysts expect its revenue to fall 5% this year, and it already owns a stake in SpaceX from last year's spectrum sale. Selling Boost would turn a shrinking business into cash or more SpaceX exposure.

Wall Street already expects a lot

Analysts expect SpaceX's revenue to climb from $48.9 billion this year to $336 billion in 2028:

SpaceX (SPCX): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2026-2028 (TIKR)

The stock traded at 48x forward earnings at Friday's close, and it's even higher after today's jump.

Boost would give SpaceX the reach Cramer is talking about, years before it could build it alone. But with T-Mobile saying no and AT&T reportedly doing the same, I'd want to see the carriers sign off before paying up for a wireless business SpaceX doesn't have yet.
